nodes.name: Trigger
nodes.notes: Entry. Inputs: content (optional — empty ⇒ fetch from WP), postId, maxInfographics (3), resolution wpBaseUrl, dryRun, replaceExisting.

nodes.name: Prepare Input
nodes.notes: Defaulty + dryRun + wpBaseUrl (input/$env).

nodes.name: Need Fetch?
nodes.notes: content empty + postId present → fetch from WP. Otherwise use the provided content

nodes.name: Fetch Post
nodes.notes: GET the current post content from WP (context=edit ⇒ content.raw). On error → empty content. Retry 3×.

nodes.name: Resolve Content
nodes.notes: Canonical content (input or Fetch Post); carries postId / resolution / wpBaseUrl / dryRun / replaceExisting downstream.

values.content: You are an infographics planner for the Polish blog biurka-regulowane.pl (client MainFlow). Analyze the article and decide which infographics would genuinely enrich it. Return STRICT JSON ONLY, no markdown, no preamble: {"graphics":[{"spec":"...","style":"...","anchor":"...","altText":"...","fileName":"..."}]}. EXISTING GRAPHICS: the article may already contain older inline infographics rendered as . Treat every such existing SVG graphic as one to MODERNIZE: for each, plan a new infographic that conveys the SAME information (read the SVG labels to learn its title, topic and numbers), and set its 'anchor' to the exact text of the H2 or H3 heading immediately above that graphic, so the new one takes its place. Cover ALL existing SVG graphics first (each becomes exactly one planned infographic). Then add infographics for other data-rich sections. AIM TO USE THE FULL MAXIMUM number of infographics whenever the article contains enough distinct data-rich sections (lists, price tiers, comparisons, steps, specifications, statistics) to justify them — a rich long article should reach the maximum. Propose fewer than the maximum only when the article genuinely lacks enough distinct material. Rules: propose between 0 and the given maximum; never exceed the maximum. 0 is valid only when the article has neither existing SVG graphics nor any lists, data or comparisons. Each infographic must cover a DIFFERENT section and a different angle (do not duplicate the same data twice). Prefer sections with price tiers, comparison tables, steps, specifications or statistics. 'spec' = a full Polish content brief for the graphic (temat, konkretne punkty, liczby, ceny, teksty do wyrenderowania), in Polish. 'style' = describe a FLAT VECTOR infographic (flat illustration, not a photo) plus the chart type (lista, proces, porownanie, statystyka, tabela), and suggest a tasteful colour palette that SUITS THE TOPIC (varied and cohesive; do NOT force a single fixed brand colour). 'anchor' = the EXACT visible TEXT of an existing H2 or H3 heading in the article (copy the heading inner text verbatim, WITHOUT any HTML tags); the heading text MUST appear literally in the article; do not use tables, paragraphs or long HTML fragments as anchors; each infographic must use a DIFFERENT heading. 'altText' = concise Polish alt text. 'fileName' = kebab-case slug ending in .png.

nodes.name: Plan Infographics
nodes.notes: gpt-4o plans max infographics as strict JSON {graphics:[{spec,style,anchor,altText,fileName}]}.

nodes.name: Parse Plan
nodes.notes: arses the plan JSON, clamps to max, validates spec+anchor. One item per graphic, or {_noGraphics:true}

nodes.name: Embed & Aggregate
nodes.notes: On Loop done: rebuilds the post content — inserts <figure> after each graphic's anchor heading (skips the RankMath TOC); replaces an old inline-SVG only when a new graphic takes its place. Returns updatedContent, inserted, skipped, mediaIds, dryRun.

nodes.name: Update Post
nodes.notes: Atomic single-request content update (only when not dry-run). Error → Build Error.

nodes.name: Summary
nodes.notes: Result: {postId, inserted, skipped, mediaIds, mode (dry-run/saved), updatedContent}.

nodes.name: Build Error
nodes.notes: On post-save failure: {success:false, error, postId, inserted, skipped}

nodes.name: Generate
nodes.notes: Calls the Infographic Generator per graphic (mode: each). onError = continueRegularOutput so failures stay on the main output (keeps the positional zip aligned)

nodes.name: Generated OK?
nodes.notes: generator success = true → Upload Media. false → Build Skip.

nodes.name: Upload Media
nodes.notes: POST the JPEG binary to WP /media; sets alt_text + title as query params in the same request. Retry 3×. Error → Build Skip.

nodes.name: Loop
nodes.notes: Single-pass barrier (batchSize 250): processes all graphics in one pass, then the done output runs Embed exactly once - including when there are 0 graphics.

nodes.name: Vars
nodes.notes: Central config: apiPrefix (/wp-json/wp/v2), used by Fetch Post and Upload Media.

nodes.name: Filter Graphics
nodes.notes: Keeps only graphics whose anchor actually resolves in the content (same findAnchorPos + TOC-skip as Embed). If none survive, emits a sentinel so the barrier loop still starts.

nodes.name: Attach Meta
nodes.notes: ositional zip of Generate's output with Filter Graphics metadata (index/anchor/altText/fileName). Workaround for the Execute-Workflow paired-item bug; preserves the infographic binary

nodes.name: Build Result
nodes.notes: Per uploaded graphic: {index, anchor, alt, mediaId, sourceUrl, status:'inserted'}. Read by Embed; returns to Loop.

nodes.name: Build Skip
nodes.notes: Per failed graphic (generation or upload): {index, anchor, status:'skipped', reason}. Returns to Loop.

nodes.name: Save?
nodes.notes: dryRun true → Summary (post NOT saved). false → Update Post.
